requirement: Annex S gathers the Edition 3 primitive encoding (Ed3 A.3), the local services (Ed3 A.2) and the raw socket server (Ed3 F.16) into one access protocol.
Hard link and expedited data encodings are dealt with in S.6.1 and S.6.2 as deprecated options.
reason: deprecated options HARD LINKS and EXPEDITED DATA (main Table 1)

requirement: SAP IDs run from 0 to 15, so at most 16 clients attach to one node's SIS.
There can be one client per SAP, which lets independent clients share the channel.
The Annex S access mechanism is mandatory, even though Annex A allows any access mechanism, so that servers and applications interoperate.
notes: is mandatory wording; Ed4 A.1.2 p.A-1 allows other mechanisms in addition.

requirement: The SIS Access Protocol is local between application and node, has no end-to-end effect, and frames each primitive so it maps directly onto a TCP stream.
The default SIS port is decimal 5066 (IANA registered).
Clients and subnetworks should be configurable to use another valid port as the default.
The server listens on the default SIS port for client connections.
notes: Listen address is our choice (localhost by default, plan 10.1); authentication NOT STATED.

requirement: The server accepts sixteen simultaneous connections so every SAP can be served.
Primitives are sent with no separators or framing beyond the generic S_Primitive elements of this annex.
No other messages pass between client and subnetwork on this connection.
Implementation-dependent management traffic may be carried inside S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST and S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION.
notes: Plan 10.1: node information via S_MANAGEMENT_MSG.

requirement: Implementation-dependent client and subnetwork communication over another socket is outside the standard and is not recommended.
notes: The operator status page (plan 10.3) is not a client interface; client-facing node information goes through S_MANAGEMENT_MSG.

requirement: Behaviour for a seventeenth or later connection is NOT STATED. Reading: accept at least sixteen connections; the one-client-per-SAP limit is enforced at bind (reject reason 3 for a SAP in use), not by refusing TCP connections.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: Closing the TCP connection is the over-TCP form of a client "physically disconnecting" [Ed4 A.2.2.2, p.A-5]. Reading: a closed connection unbinds its client and frees its SAP at once, with no S_UNBIND_INDICATION.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The main purpose of the protocol is client access to the Annex A core SIS services.

Local management and flow control primitives (table printed as "Table A-1"): SIS to client S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY, S_DATA_FLOW_ON, S_DATA_FLOW_OFF, S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION; client to SIS S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST; S_KEEP_ALIVE both ways.
notes: Table label duplicates Annex A's Table A-1 (editorial).

requirement: The SIS issues S_DATA_FLOW_ON and S_DATA_FLOW_OFF to control the client's transfer of U_PDUs.
On S_DATA_FLOW_OFF the client stops sending U_PDUs.
notes: Client duty (client library).

requirement: Once the client has received S_DATA_FLOW_ON, it is allowed to send U_PDUs again.
notes: Client duty.

requirement: The SIS may use these primitives or other mechanisms to throttle local clients.
U_PDUs a client sends after being sent S_DATA_FLOW_OFF may be discarded with no acknowledgement, indication or warning.
notes: See interp below for our choice.

requirement: A client never controls the flow of data from the subnetwork, explicitly or implicitly.
notes: Client duty: always keep reading the socket.

requirement: Every client is ready at all times to accept data the node receives for it.
notes: Client duty.

requirement: The node may disconnect a client that does not accept data.
notes: Host side (P6-3), with interp S-0029: the core never sees socket writes.

requirement: The flow state after bind is NOT STATED. Reading: flow is on once S_BIND_ACCEPTED is sent; the node sends no S_DATA_FLOW_ON at bind and sends S_DATA_FLOW_OFF only when it needs to throttle.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: S.4.1 lets the node silently discard U_PDUs sent after S_DATA_FLOW_OFF. Reading: the node keeps reading the socket; such a U_PDU is discarded, and if it asked for delivery confirmation the client gets S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED with reason 13 (Data Buffers Full).
notes: Our choice within the may. The over-MTU, delivery mode and broadcast checks of S-0161 come first (interp S-0163).

requirement: How the node detects a client that is not reading is NOT STATED. Reading: if data queued for a client cannot be written to its connection within a fixed time bound, or more than a fixed number of bytes is waiting to be written to it, the node closes the connection, which unbinds the client and frees its SAP.
notes: Bounds fixed in code, 30 s and 1 MiB (core-architecture.md 12.7), documented; no setting (no-unrequested-settings rule). Host side (P6-3): the core never sees socket writes. Byte bound added by issue #80.

requirement: A client sends a management message to the subnetwork with S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST.
The content of the management message is implementation-dependent and not specified (for example commands such as go to EMCON, or requests for statistics).
A minimally compliant subnetwork can receive S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST, with no duty to act on it.
Management coordination between peer nodes over the air uses the UNIDATA primitives, not this primitive.
notes: Management messages are local only; the node never puts one on air.

requirement: The subnetwork sends a management message to a client with S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION.
The content of the management indication is implementation-dependent and not specified.
notes: We publish our encoding (plan 10.1): MSG TYPE 1 (interp J-0082), MSG TYPE 2 (interp S-0164).

requirement: A minimally compliant client can receive S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION, with no duty to act on it.
notes: Client duty.

requirement: The indication may answer a request or be sent unprompted.

MSG TYPE and MSG BODY encodings are implementation-dependent [Ed4 S.4.2, S.4.3, S.5.11]. Reading: the node answers its own published request types (node information such as own address, per-peer rate and SNR); a request with an unknown MSG TYPE is ignored without reply and does not count as an invalid primitive.
notes: Plan 10.1. The published request type is MSG TYPE 2, node information (interp S-0164).

requirement: Either client or SIS may send S_KEEP_ALIVE, for example when idle, to check the connection is alive.
A minimally compliant client or SIS need not generate S_KEEP_ALIVE except to answer one.
A received S_KEEP_ALIVE is answered with S_KEEP_ALIVE within 10 seconds.
notes: Shall number (1) missing in the source.

requirement: If the answer cannot be sent within 10 seconds, none is sent.
No more than one S_KEEP_ALIVE is sent to the same destination in any 120 seconds.

The 10 s answer duty and the 120 s sending limit clash when a peer sends keep-alives more often than every 120 s. Reading: an answer is always sent (within 10 s) and the 120 s limit governs only unprompted keep-alives; unprompted ones are also spaced at least 120 s from any keep-alive already sent to that destination.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The trigger for unbind reason 2 (Inactivity, no answer to keep-alive) [Ed4 A.2.2.5, p.A-7] is NOT STATED. Reading: the node sends no unprompted keep-alives and relies on TCP connection state; it never sends unbind reason 2. The client library may probe the node within the 120 s limit.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY may be sent at any time to all or some clients when the node's status changes (for example EMCON, or bandwidth reserved for others).
notes: The node never sends it (interp S-0165).

requirement: The content of S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY is implementation-dependent.
notes: Contradicted by the value tables on the same page; see interp.

requirement: A minimally compliant client can receive S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY, with no duty to act on it.
notes: Client duty.

requirement: Node Status values: 0 OFF, 1 ON, 2 Receive-Only, 3 Half-Duplex, 4 Full-Duplex, 5 Transmit-Only.
For any node status except ON, the Reason argument gives the cause, coded 0 unspecified, 1 Local Node in EMCON, 2 Reserved.
notes: Never sent (interp S-0165); the codec carries the values.

requirement: The Node Status values above are the ones used in the Annex S encoding.
notes: Source says "represent the reason" for status values (editorial).

requirement: The Reason values above are the ones used in the Annex S encoding.

S.4.5 prints Node Status and Reason value tables that "shall" be used [p.S-7], while S.4.5 and S.5.8 call the content implementation-dependent [pp.S-7, S-14]. Reading: the node sends only the S.4.5 values; the client library accepts any value and treats unknown ones as unspecified.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. Node side: nothing is sent (interp S-0165); the client library half is P6-3.

requirement: Primitives are encoded as given in the text and figures of S.5.
Unless stated otherwise, argument values are encoded into their fields per CCITT V.42 8.1.2.3.
In a field within one octet, the lowest-numbered bit is the least significant.
In a field spanning octets, significance falls as octet number rises: multi-byte values are sent most significant byte first.
notes: Big-endian; the preamble is the one exception (S.5.2).

requirement: Each 4-byte address field carries the 3.5-byte address plus the size information of S.5.16.1.
The address's lowest-order bit sits in the field's lowest-order position (normally bit 0 of the highest-numbered byte), matching the D_PDU address mapping of C.3.2.6.
notes: Right-aligned. Conflicts with Fig S-19; see interp at S.5.16.1.

requirement: Every primitive is the sequence: 2-byte preamble, 1-byte version, 2-byte size, then the primitive body.
notes: Fig S-3. Source refers to "Figure A-1(a)", the Ed3 number (editorial).

requirement: The preamble is the 16-bit Maury-Styles sequence 0xEB90, sent least significant bit first.
Preamble byte 0 holds the low-order bits of the sequence: 0x90.
notes: Fig S-4.

requirement: Preamble byte 1 holds the high-order bits of the sequence: 0xEB.
notes: So the wire bytes are 90 EB.

requirement: The preamble byte order is an exception to the general field rule of S.5.1.
The byte after the preamble is the version number.
The version number is 0x00 for this edition.
notes: Same as Ed1 and Ed3; no in-band edition signal.

requirement: The next two bytes give the size in bytes of the primitive body that follows (type byte onward), excluding preamble, version and size.
The size's least significant bit is in the low-order bit of the low-order byte: byte 3 is the high byte, byte 4 the low byte.
notes: Shall number (8) missing in the source.

requirement: The primitive body is at least one byte (size >= 1).
notes: Fig S-3.

requirement: Bits of each byte are transmitted least significant first, per CCITT V.42 8.1.2.2.
notes: No effect over a TCP byte stream.

requirement: Byte 5, the first body byte, is the primitive type number.
notes: Shall number (12) missing; (13) used twice.

requirement: Remaining body bytes follow in order, each least significant bit first, as defined for each primitive.
Bits marked NOT USED are sent as 0 unless a primitive says otherwise.
Handling of received NOT USED bits that are not 0 is NOT STATED. Reading: ignore them.
Handling of a bad preamble, a non-zero version or a zero size is NOT STATED. Reading: count one invalid primitive, then scan forward byte by byte for the next 90 EB preamble and resume there.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: Handling of a primitive whose size does not match its type's layout (for example a U_PDU size field that disagrees with the frame size) is NOT STATED. Reading: skip the framed body by its size field and count one invalid primitive; an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST whose U_PDU merely exceeds the MTU is instead rejected with reason 4.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: Too many invalid primitives (unbind reason 3) has no stated threshold [Ed4 A.2.2.5, p.A-7]. Reading: after 10 invalid primitives on one connection with no valid primitive in between, the node sends S_UNBIND_INDICATION reason 3 (if bound) and closes the connection.
notes: Fixed constant, no setting. Unknown type numbers, deprecated types and primitives in the wrong direction count as invalid.

requirement: S_BIND_REQUEST body is 4 bytes: byte 5 type 1; byte 6 SAP ID (bits 7 to 4) and RANK (bits 3 to 0); byte 7 Service Type bits 11 to 4; byte 8 Service Type bits 3 to 0 in bits 7 to 4, bits 3 to 0 NOT USED.
notes: Fig S-5.

requirement: The 12-bit Service Type has five subfields: Transmission Mode (byte 7 bits 7 to 4), Delivery Confirmation (byte 7 bits 3 to 2), Delivery Order (byte 7 bit 1), Extended Field (byte 7 bit 0), Minimum Number of Retransmissions (byte 8 bits 7 to 4).
notes: Fig S-6, read from rendered page.

requirement: Transmission Mode values: 0 ignore service type field, 1 ARQ, 2 non-ARQ (for example broadcast), 3 non-ARQ with errors, 4 and up to be defined.
notes: We accept only 1 and 2 at bind (interp below).

requirement: Delivery Confirmation values: 00 none, 01 node delivery, 10 client delivery, 11 not defined.
Delivery Order values: 0 in-order delivery, 1 as they arrive.
Extended Field values: 0 no extended field, 1 extended field follows.
Minimum Number of Retransmissions is used only when Transmission Mode is a non-ARQ subtype and is "don't care" otherwise.
notes: 4-bit field, 0 to 15.

requirement: The Service Type gives the client's requested default service.
The Service Type applies to every U_PDU the client submits until it unbinds, unless overridden by a U_PDU's Delivery Mode.
The only way a client changes its default service type is to unbind and then bind again.
notes: Client duty; node rejects a second bind on a bound connection (interp below).

requirement: RANK, an Edition 3 field unused in Edition 4, is sent as 0 and ignored on receipt.
The Service Type states ARQ or non-ARQ, with a non-ARQ submode when non-ARQ.
Transmission Mode 0 is invalid in a bind.
The client requests exactly one delivery confirmation mode: none, node-to-node or client-to-client.
Explicit delivery confirmation is requested only with ARQ.
notes: Same rule as Ed4 A.2.2.6.

requirement: The client requests in-order delivery or delivery in arrival order.
notes: A.2.2.6 forbids in-order with non-ARQ.

requirement: The Extended Field is set to 0; its use is undefined.
Minimum Number of Retransmissions is valid only when Transmission Mode is non-ARQ.
For non-ARQ, the subnetwork retransmits each U_PDU the given number of times.
notes: N+1 transmissions in total (interp in A matrix at A.2.2.6). P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; the repeats are P3-4.

requirement: The retransmission count may be 0, meaning the U_PDU is sent once.
notes: P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; sending is P3-4.

requirement: The node's response to an invalid bind Service Type is NOT STATED, and no bind reject reason fits [Ed4 A.2.2.4, p.A-6]. Reading: reject with S_BIND_REJECTED reason 1 (Not Enough Resources) when Transmission Mode is 0, 3 or 4 and up, Delivery Confirmation is 11, confirmation is asked with non-ARQ, or Extended Field is 1. Non-ARQ with in-order delivery is accepted and treated as arrival order, since Ed3 clients could send it.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. Mode 3 is the unsupported NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS option.

requirement: A second S_BIND_REQUEST on a connection that is already bound is NOT STATED. Reading: reject it with S_BIND_REJECTED reason 3 (SAP ID already allocated) and keep the existing binding.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: Primitives received before a successful bind are NOT STATED beyond "cannot be serviced" [Ed4 A.2.2.1, p.A-4]. Reading: S_UNIDATA_REQUEST before bind is discarded and counts as an invalid primitive; S_KEEP_ALIVE and S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST are handled normally before bind.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: S_UNBIND_REQUEST body is 1 byte: type 2.
notes: Fig S-7.

requirement: Whether the node closes the TCP connection after S_UNBIND_REQUEST or S_UNBIND_INDICATION is NOT STATED. Reading: keep it open so the client may bind again [Ed4 A.2.2.2, p.A-5]; only on shutdown (unbind reason 6) or the invalid-primitive limit does the node close it.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: S_BIND_ACCEPTED body is 4 bytes: byte 5 type 3; byte 6 SAP ID (bits 7 to 4), bits 3 to 0 NOT USED; bytes 7 and 8 MTU, most significant byte first.
S_BIND_REJECTED body is 2 bytes: byte 5 type 4; byte 6 REASON.
notes: Fig S-9.

requirement: The REASON takes a value from Annex A A.2.2.4.
S_UNBIND_INDICATION body is 2 bytes: byte 5 type 5; byte 6 REASON.
notes: Fig S-10.

requirement: The REASON takes a value from Annex A A.2.2.5.
S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY body is 3 bytes: byte 5 type 14; byte 6 NODE STATUS; byte 7 REASON.
notes: Fig S-11.

requirement: The encoding of NODE STATUS and REASON is implementation-dependent.
notes: See interp at S.4.5.

requirement: S_DATA_FLOW_ON and S_DATA_FLOW_OFF bodies are 1 byte each, the type number; S_DATA_FLOW_ON is 15.
notes: Fig S-12.

requirement: Fig S-12 prints S_DATA_FLOW_OFF as type 15, the same as S_DATA_FLOW_ON. Reading: S_DATA_FLOW_OFF is 16, as in Ed1 Fig A-17, since Annex S says the protocol is unchanged from Edition 3 [Ed4 S.7, p.S-21].
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: S_KEEP_ALIVE body is 1 byte: type 17.
notes: Fig S-13 caption wrongly names the flow primitives (editorial).

requirement: S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST (type 18) and S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION (type 19) are variable length: byte 5 type; byte 6 MSG TYPE; bytes 7 onward MSG BODY.
notes: Fig S-14. Body length follows from the frame size.

requirement: MSG TYPE and MSG BODY encodings are implementation-dependent.

S_UNIDATA_REQUEST is variable length: byte 5 type 20; byte 6 PRIORITY (bits 7 to 4) and DESTINATION SAP ID (bits 3 to 0); bytes 7 to 10 DESTINATION NODE ADDRESS; byte 11 DELIVERY MODE bits 11 to 4; byte 12 DELIVERY MODE bits 3 to 0 (bits 7 to 4) and TTL bits 19 to 16 (bits 3 to 0); bytes 13 and 14 TTL bits 15 to 0; bytes 15 and 16 U_PDU size; bytes 17 onward the U_PDU.
notes: Fig S-15, read from rendered page.

requirement: TTL is 20 bits in units of 2 seconds, maximum field value 648000 (about 15 days), with its LSB at the LSB of byte 14.
The U_PDU in S_UNIDATA_REQUEST may be zero bytes long (size >= 0).
Node address fields are encoded per S.5.16.1.
S.5.12 refers to SOURCE and DESTINATION NODE ADDRESS fields, but Fig S-15 has no source address. Reading: the request carries only a destination address; the source is the local node's address.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The DELIVERY MODE field is encoded per S.5.16.2.
Handling of a TTL field above 648000 (the 20-bit field can hold up to 1048575) is NOT STATED. Reading: treat it as 648000.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: S_UNIDATA_INDICATION is variable length: byte 5 type 21; byte 6 PRIORITY (bits 7 to 4) and DESTINATION SAP ID (bits 3 to 0); bytes 7 to 10 DESTINATION NODE ADDRESS; byte 11 TRANSMISSION MODE (bits 7 to 4) and SOURCE SAP ID (bits 3 to 0); bytes 12 to 15 SOURCE NODE ADDRESS; bytes 16 and 17 U_PDU size N; then the U_PDU (from byte 18 when no error fields are present).
notes: Fig S-16, read from rendered page.

requirement: The error fields (2-byte errored-block count K, K pairs of 2-byte pointer and 2-byte size, 2-byte non-received count L, L such pairs) are present only when the transmission mode is non-ARQ with errors, and are omitted otherwise.
notes: We always omit them.

requirement: When present, the error fields sit between the U_PDU size and the U_PDU.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Source and destination node address fields are encoded per S.5.16.1.
The TRANSMISSION MODE field is encoded per S.5.16.3.

S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_CONFIRM is variable length: byte 5 type 22; byte 6 NOT USED (bits 7 to 4) and DESTINATION SAP ID (bits 3 to 0); bytes 7 to 10 DESTINATION NODE ADDRESS; bytes 11 and 12 size of the confirmed U_PDU or part; bytes 13 onward that U_PDU or part.
notes: Fig S-17.

requirement: The destination address field is encoded per S.5.16.1.

S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED is variable length: byte 5 type 23; byte 6 REASON (bits 7 to 4) and DESTINATION SAP ID (bits 3 to 0); bytes 7 to 10 DESTINATION NODE ADDRESS; bytes 11 and 12 size of the rejected U_PDU or part; bytes 13 onward that U_PDU or part.
notes: Fig S-18. REASON is 4 bits, values 1 to 15.

requirement: The destination address field is encoded per S.5.16.1.
The REASON takes a value from Annex A A.2.2.8.
S.5.16 adds detail on arguments common to several primitives.
Node addresses are encoded in formats that are multiples of 4 bits, per Fig S-19.
notes: Applies to all UNIDATA primitives.

requirement: Address field layout (Fig S-19): first byte bits 7 to 5 the address size in half-bytes (up to 7), bit 4 the group flag (0 individual, 1 group), then 28 address bits; only the first SIZE half-bytes are valid and the rest are don't care.
notes: Rendered page checked.

requirement: Group addresses appear only as the destination of non-ARQ PDUs.
ARQ destination SAPs and addresses, and source SAPs and addresses of all PDUs, are individual.

Address alignment: S.5.1 places the address LSB at bit 0 of the last byte (right-aligned) [p.S-8], but Fig S-19 says only the first SIZE half-bytes are valid [p.S-19]. Reading: send right-aligned with SIZE = 7 and unused nibbles 0, so both readings agree; decode right-aligned.
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: The node's response to an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST that sends ARQ (explicitly or by default) to a group address is NOT STATED. Reading: reject with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reason 6 (Broadcast Not Allowed), whether or not confirmation was requested.
notes: Not in plan 4.4.

requirement: The DELIVERY MODE argument is encoded per Fig S-20: the same 12-bit subfield layout as the bind Service Type.
notes: Bytes 11 and 12 of S_UNIDATA_REQUEST.

requirement: With DELIVERY MODE DEFAULT, the U_PDU uses the Service Type from the client's S_BIND_REQUEST.
A non-DEFAULT DELIVERY MODE overrides the bind Service Type for that U_PDU.
Transmission Mode 0 in DELIVERY MODE means DEFAULT.
When DELIVERY MODE is DEFAULT, all its other subfields are ignored.
Per-U_PDU delivery confirmation may be none, node-to-node or client-to-client.
A client may ask per U_PDU for in-order delivery or delivery in arrival order.
notes: In-order is forbidden with non-ARQ (Ed4 A.2.2.6).

requirement: The DELIVERY MODE Extended Field is set to 0.
Minimum Number of Retransmissions is valid only when Transmission Mode is a non-ARQ type or subtype.
For non-ARQ, the subnetwork retransmits each U_PDU the given number of times.
notes: N+1 in total (A matrix interp). P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; the repeats are P3-4.

requirement: The retransmission count may be 0, meaning the U_PDU is sent once.
notes: P3-1 carries the count to the DTS; sending is P3-4.

requirement: The node's response to an invalid non-DEFAULT DELIVERY MODE is NOT STATED. Reading: reject with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED reason 5 (Tx Mode not specified), whether or not confirmation was requested, when Transmission Mode is 3 or 4 and up, Delivery Confirmation is 11, confirmation is asked with non-ARQ, or Extended Field is 1. Non-ARQ with in-order is accepted and sent as arrival order.
notes: Not in plan 4.4. Mirrors the bind interp at S.5.3.

requirement: The TRANSMISSION MODE in S_UNIDATA_INDICATION is encoded per Fig S-21, in byte 11 bits 7 to 4.
Indication Transmission Mode values: 0 not used, 1 ARQ, 2 non-ARQ (broadcast), 3 non-ARQ with errors, 4 and up to be defined.
notes: We send only 1 or 2.

requirement: The low four bits of that byte carry the SOURCE SAP ID.
Hard links and expedited data are optional, deprecated, specified by reference to Edition 3, and expected to be removed.
HARD LINKS option primitives are encoded per Edition 3 Annex A section A.3; Rank may be needed.
notes: Plan 4.3: types 6 to 13 received are invalid primitives.

requirement: EXPEDITED DATA option primitives are encoded per Edition 3 Annex A section A.3.
notes: Plan 4.3: types 24 to 27 received are invalid primitives.

requirement: A received deprecated primitive (hard link types 6 to 13, expedited types 24 to 27) is not covered by Ed4. Reading: treat it as an invalid primitive; repeated ones lead to unbind reason 3.
notes: Plan 4.3 last row.

requirement: The access protocol is unchanged from Edition 3; Annex S does not specify the hard link and expedited protocol elements, which exist only in Edition 3.
notes: Basis for the FLOW_OFF = 16 reading.

requirement: Resynchronising the byte stream after an invalid primitive is NOT STATED beyond S-0075 and S-0076, and nor is a type byte that names no primitive (0, 28 and up). Reading: a run of bytes not at a 90 EB preamble counts as one invalid primitive however long it is; after a bad version or zero size the scan for the next 90 EB restarts at the byte after the first preamble byte, and the bytes it passes over count for nothing more; a deprecated type, an unknown type or a body of the wrong length is skipped by its size field once the whole body has arrived. A partial frame is held, with no error, until it completes.
notes: corpus-format.md section 3.7. Accepted by the coordinator in the phase 1d review.

requirement: An S_UNBIND_REQUEST from a client that is not bound is NOT STATED [Ed4 A.2.2.2, p.A-5; S.5.4, p.S-12]. Reading: discard it with no reply and count it as an invalid primitive, as S-0100 does for S_UNIDATA_REQUEST before bind.
notes: Added by P3-1.

requirement: Which reason the node sends when several bind or unidata checks fail at once is NOT STATED [Ed4 A.2.2.4, p.A-6; A.2.2.8, p.A-10; S.5.3, p.S-11; S.5.16, pp.S-19 to S-20]. Reading: a bind is checked for an existing binding on the connection (reason 3, S-0099), then the Service Type (reason 1, S-0098), then the SAP in use by another client (reason 3); an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST from a bound client is checked for a U_PDU over the MTU (reason 4, A-0115), then the DELIVERY MODE (reason 5, S-0150), then ARQ to a group address (reason 6, S-0138). The first failure decides.
notes: Added by P3-1.

requirement: S-0077 restarts the invalid-primitive count at a valid primitive but does not say whether a request the node refuses is valid [Ed4 A.2.2.5, p.A-7]. Reading: a client-to-node primitive that decodes and is acted on is valid, including an S_BIND_REQUEST answered with S_BIND_REJECTED and an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST answered with S_UNIDATA_REQUEST_REJECTED. Invalid are the framing errors (S-0075, S-0076, S-0159), deprecated and unknown types (S-0157, S-0159), node-to-client types sent by a client (S-0077), and primitives before bind (S-0100, S-0160).
notes: Added by P3-1.

requirement: When the node sends S_DATA_FLOW_OFF and S_DATA_FLOW_ON is NOT STATED; Annex B and C only ask that SIS flow control keep DTS queues short [Ed4 S.4.1, p.S-5; B.7.2.8, p.B-35; C.1.5, p.C-3]. Reading: each client U_PDU the node accepts counts its U_PDU bytes against its client until the lower sublayers are finished with it: confirmed or rejected by the CAS (for non-ARQ, see interp C-1255), or dropped by the SIS while held for a soft link. The node sends S_DATA_FLOW_OFF after accepting a U_PDU that brings the client to 16384 bytes (eight MTUs) or more, and S_DATA_FLOW_ON when the count falls to 8192 bytes (four MTUs) or less. While flow is off a U_PDU that passes the S-0161 checks is discarded (S-0028). The count and the flow state go with the binding: an unbind or disconnect clears them, and a new binding starts with flow on and nothing counted (S-0027). Client confirmations the SIS sends for its peers do not count.
notes: S-0019, S-0022, S-0023, S-0027, S-0028, B-0279, C-0019, C-0020. Thresholds fixed in code, not settings (no-unrequested-settings rule); T4 may retune them. Per client, so one busy client never holds off another.

requirement: S-0038 says the node answers its own published request types but the encoding is ours [Ed4 S.4.2, S.4.3, pp.S-5 to S-6; S.5.11, p.S-15]. Reading: S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_REQUEST MSG TYPE 2 asks for node information; its body is ignored, and the node answers at once, to the asking connection only and whether or not it is bound, with S_MANAGEMENT_MSG_INDICATION MSG TYPE 2. Body: this node's 4-byte address field (Fig S-19, SIZE 7), the transmit waveform number and interleaver code (0 ultra short to 5 very long), a one-byte peer count, then up to 255 13-byte records in address order, one per peer with a receive quality record (C-0833) or a soft link record: address field; soft link state (0 none, 1 being made or held off, 2 established, 3 closing); transmit waveform and interleaver to the peer; waveform and interleaver of the last burst heard from it (0xFF when never heard); its SNR in tenths of a dB, signed 16-bit big-endian (0x8000 when not given or never heard); whole seconds since that burst ended, big-endian, saturating at 65534 (0xFFFF when never heard).
notes: Plan 10.1 (own address, rate and SNR per peer). The transmit speed is drc.default_speed for every peer until phase 7; the field is per peer so the format does not change then.

requirement: S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY may be sent when the node's status changes [Ed4 S.4.5, p.S-7]. Reading: the node's status never changes while it runs (it has no EMCON, receive-only or other mode, and shutdown is told by unbind reason 6, A-0059), so it never sends S_SUBNET_AVAILABILITY.
notes: S-0046 to S-0053. A later phase that adds EMCON or a receive-only mode sends it on each change, with the S.4.5 values (S-0053).

requirement: A largest S_Primitive size, or a size check that lets a receiver treat an implausible size field as a framing error, is NOT STATED: the only limit is the two-byte Size_of_Primitive field [Ed4 S.5.2, pp.S-9 to S-10]. Reading: a receiver accepts any size from 1 to 65535 and holds a partial frame until it completes (S-0159), with no smaller limit, because an S_UNIDATA_REQUEST whose U_PDU exceeds the MTU must be read whole to be rejected with reason 4 [Ed4 A.2.2.3, p.A-6; A.2.2.8, p.A-10]. So a corrupt size field can hold up to 65535 bytes of the stream before the frame is judged and skipped.
notes: Issue #80 (P6-3a review): no behaviour change. T2 sis-unidata-over-mtu relies on it.
